newsitem.title: FINLAND: Nokia sends lively Helsinki to 12-month high.
newsitem.headline: Nokia sends lively Helsinki to 12-month high.

text.p: Shares ended a lively session at their highest level since September 26, 1995, boosted by a rally in Nokia after the telecoms major said it sealed a big mobile phone deal in the U.S.
The HEX index rose 0.52 percent to 2,202.81. Volume was hefty at 507 million markka.
Nokia closed up 7.70 markka at 210.00, a nine-month high. The share rose sharply after Nokia announced a $240 million handset deal with AT&T, which analysts called "a breakthrough" for Nokia.
Trade in Nokia was heavy, accounting for 50 percent of total bourse volume.
Forestries were out of focus and softened on the sector's uncertain outlook, brokers said.
The forestry sub-index fell 0.55 percent, with UPM-Kymmene losing 0.70 markka to close at 95.80 and Enso shedding 0.20 to 36.50 markka.
Chemicals group Kemira slipped 0.30 markka to 52.20 in fair trade after releasing January-August profits largely in line with expectations.
Shares in medical equipment maker Instrumentarium gained slightly ahead of eight-month results due to be released on Friday at 0830/0530 GMT, but trade in the share was thin.
Electronics component maker Aspoyhtyma tracked Nokia and closed fair trade 6.90 markka higher at 159.00.
The generally upbeat tone was somewhat dampened by losses in metal and financial industry shares as investors took profits after recent gains.
"The market may be be wary ahead of U.S. jobless data due on Friday," one broker said.
